title.en: Adding and subtracting up to 200 (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en: Four sets of number cards 1 to 10 are shuffled and spread out face down. Children open one card at a time; if any three open cards make an addition or subtraction fact like 2, 4 and 6, they keep all three.

Let us play the card game from the book. Make four sets of number cards 1 to 10.
Shuffle and spread them facing down. Open one card at a time.
If three open cards make an addition or subtraction fact, such as 2 + 4 = 6, you keep them.
Number facts help when we add and subtract bigger numbers.
(additional, not in the textbook) We can add bigger numbers using tens and ones. 45 + 30 is 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens and 5 ones, so 75.
(additional, not in the textbook) To subtract, take away tens from tens and ones from ones. 86 - 20 = 66.

prompt.en: Why do we add tens with tens?

requiredIdeas.en: They are the same kind of unit

points.en: Three cards can make a fact.
Add tens to tens and ones to ones.
